what_happened: A docs job to add a README section saying all of Athena's design is changeable was rejected at final verification. One of 6 acceptance criteria was unmet: the section must name the exceptions that actually exist (BRIEF.md, changed only by Sri, and records/, immutable), with links that resolve. The verifier raised one major finding. The section (README.md:252, "Two things are not open to a job", and the CHANGELOG.md:13-14 entry) says only two things are off-limits. Admission also blocks owner-private and read-only paths and changes to path classification. So the list of exceptions is incomplete and the claim of "two" is false. No failed checks are listed.
cause: The exception list was written from the request's wording and memory, not from the admission rules that define what a job may not touch. The reading's criterion itself named only BRIEF.md and records/, so it fixed the incomplete set as the standard. Nothing makes a doc that states a rule or limit be cross-checked against the code or config that enforces it. Only the final verifier compared the claim to admission, after all spend.
prevention: When a reading's deliverable states a limit, exception or "only N" claim about Athena's behavior, require the reading and plan to derive the list from the enforcing source (the admission path classification code and config) and cite it. Add a criterion that each listed item maps to that source and that the doc does not say "only" or give a count unless the count is derived from it. This check would run before the producer, so an incomplete list is caught early.
proposed_request: Fix the README section on what a job may change so it lists every limit that admission enforces. Read the admission path classification in the code and config first, and list each kind of path a job cannot change: BRIEF.md (changed only by Sri), records/ (immutable), owner-private paths, read-only paths, and changes to path classification itself. Link each to where it is stated, and make sure each link resolves. Do not say "two things" or give any count unless it matches that source. Update the matching CHANGELOG.md entry to say the same. Acceptance: every path class admission refuses appears in the section; the wording gives no count that disagrees with admission; the links resolve to existing files; cargo test passes.
